display.title: Episode 448: The Mountain of Ice (Sukkos and Simchas Torah)
display.summary_short: On Chol HaMoed Sukkos, Uncle Yossi explains how the Torah dances with us on Simchas Torah, and tells how Rabbi Meir of Premishlan walked down icy steps without slipping.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5751. Uncle Yossi explains 'vesamachta bechagecha': Sukkos is our very own holiday, full of reasons for joy, from the sukkah and the four kinds to the Ushpizin. On Simchas Torah we dance with the Torah, and since the Torah has no feet or hands, it asks to join our dance and blesses us with health; even the youngest can hold on to the handles or the mantle. A seven-year-old yeshiva boy who loves saying the Twelve Pesukim recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: in Premishlan the mikvah stood on top of a steep hill, and in winter only Rabbi Meir could walk down the icy steps. Two visiting businessmen mock this and try it themselves, tumbling to the bottom. The townspeople kindly care for them, and when they come to apologize, Rabbi Meir explains that whoever is tied to the One above does not fall. Uncle Yossi invites children to write in about their Hakafos.
display.lesson: Hold on tightly to Hashem through Torah and mitzvos, and you will not fall.
